correctness.rationale: For a fixed received word, the rightmost insertion representatives are the two appends and the insertion opposite to the symbol at each of the n−1 other positions, giving n+1 distinct parents. Deleting positions i and j from the same parent gives the same output only if entries i through j are constant; thus each parent's deletion set is an interval. The n edges each flip exactly the corresponding check coordinate and consecutive edges share a parent, so the edge syndromes recover the mask as the XOR of odd-parent intervals. Its 2r padded boundaries require at least r odd parents. For the proposed y the prescribed symbols do not conflict even with a single zero between support runs. The selected intervals reproduce those edge syndromes, and the actual syndrome of X_1 is r−1+Σ_j ℓ_j t_j=1 mod 2, ruling out global complement. For a single even run one odd parent alone would have to be constant on the whole support and would in fact be even. The block of ℓ−2 ones gives exactly two odd parents, including the ℓ=2 case. Unique tiling by 0 and 11 gives F_{n+1}, including the zero mask. Read the frozen proof, checker and recorded output; independently tested all masks and outputs through n=8 by canonical rightmost insertions with `python /workspace/branches/review-computations/check_finite.py`. The finite run corroborates the all-length argument, and does not classify the exceptional masks.
